Thomas P. Stafford: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1930–2024)

Set to become just the fourth queen to rule her Scandinavian kingdom in her own right — and the first since 1720 — she is heir apparent thanks to a 1980 law that was Western Europe's first with absolute primogeniture. Who is she?
Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden: Heir apparent to the Swedish throne (born 1977)
Fought along the Suez Canal from 1967 to 1970 after Arab leaders adopted the 'three no's' policy, this conflict pitted Israel against Egypt, Jordan, and the PLO?
War of Attrition: 1967–1970 war between Israel and Egypt. Following the 1967 Six-Day War, no serious diplomatic efforts were made to resolve the issues at the heart of the Arab–Israeli conflict.
It's the season that arrives when your hemisphere tilts away from the Sun, so that while one half of Earth shivers the other basks in summer. Which season?
Winter: Coldest of the four temperate seasons.
This Japanese samurai, who lived from 1574 to 1607, served as daimyō of the Fukui Domain in Echizen during the transition into the Edo period — who is he?
Yūki Hideyasu: Japanese samurai. Yūki Hideyasu (結城 秀康; 1 March 1574 – 2 June 1607) was a Japanese samurai who lived during the Azuchi–Momoyama and early Edo periods.
Which one below was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Anna Atkins (born 1799) is the earliest of the four. Anna Atkins (née Children; 16 March 1799 – 9 June 1871) was an English botanist and photographer.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Zhuge Liang (born 181) is the earliest of the four. After helping found Shu Han, Zhuge Liang exercised near-total authority over both civil and military affairs.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Aryabhata is an astronomer. The claim that Nalanda used to be located in Kusamapura/Pataliputra also cannot be proven.
Who among these is a mathematician?
John Horton Conway is a mathematician. John Horton Conway (26 December 1937 – 11 April 2020) was an English mathematician.
What is the atomic number of Caesium?
Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
What is the atomic number of Tungsten?
Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
In what year did Hamish Harding die?
Hamish Harding: George Hamish Livingston Harding (24 June 1964 – 18 June 2023) was a British businessman, pilot and adventurer based in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
In what year was Pluto discovered?
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
TypeScript: Anders Hejlsberg. TypeScript (TS) is a high-level programming language that adds static typing with optional type annotations to JavaScript.
Pethidine: Pfizer. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.
Who is credited with discovering Archaeopteryx?
Archaeopteryx: Carl Friedrich Häberlein. Archaeopteryx (lit. 'ancient wing'), sometimes referred to by its German name, "Urvogel " (lit. 'Primeval Bird') is an extinct genus of bird-like dinosaurs.
Who is credited with discovering Oganesson?
Oganesson: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
Who is credited with discovering Cimetidine?
Cimetidine: John Colin Emmett. Cimetidine, sold under the brand name Tagamet among others, is a histamine H2 receptor antagonist that inhibits stomach acid production.
Who is credited with discovering Iridium?
Iridium: Smithson Tennant. Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.
A broad-spectrum benzimidazole drug, this medicine clears intestinal parasites from pinworm to hookworm to tapeworm — which agent is it?
Albendazole is a broad-spectrum antihelmintic and antiprotozoal agent of the benzimidazole type.
A balloon-like bulge at a weakened patch of vessel wall, it can turn lethal in the brain's circle of Willis or the aorta if it bursts — what is this?
Aneurysm is an outward bulging, likened to a bubble or balloon, caused by a localized, abnormal, weak spot on a blood vessel wall.
Founder of a prominent Russian design studio and an avid, famously foul-mouthed blogger, this designer and entrepreneur is also a member of the Tolstoy family — name this designer?
Artemy Lebedev (born 13 February 1975) is a Russian designer, entrepreneur and Internet personality.
Built under license from the Swiss Pilatus PC-9, this turboprop trainer serves the US Air Force, Navy, and Marine Corps and flies in Canada under the designation CT-156 Harvard — which aircraft?
Beechcraft T-6 Texan II is a single-engined, turboprop aircraft currently built by Textron Aviation, formerly manufactured by Raytheon Aircraft Company, which sold to Textron in 2007.
Born as Hughes Helicopters' Model 77 to replace the AH-1 Cobra, this twin-turboshaft attack helicopter packs a 30 mm chain gun and Hellfire missiles in a tandem cockpit — what is it?
Boeing AH-64 Apache (-) is an American twin-turboshaft attack helicopter with a tailwheel-type landing gear and a tandem cockpit for a crew of two.

Synthesized by the liver in response to inflammation, this ring-shaped blood molecule binds to the surface of dead or dying cells to activate the immune system's complement cascade. What is it commonly called?
C-reactive protein (CRP) is an annular (ring-shaped) pentameric protein found in blood plasma, whose circulating concentration rises in response to inflammation.
Which metabolic process is the polar opposite of anabolism, breaking large molecules such as proteins and lipids down into monomers while releasing energy, some of it lost as heat?
Catabolism is the set of metabolic pathways that breaks down molecules into smaller units that are either oxidized to release energy or used in other anabolic reactions.
Linked to repeated head trauma, this worsening neurodegenerative disease turns up in boxers and footballers — and even in soccer players, largely from heading the ball. What is it?

Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a neurodegenerative disease linked to repeated trauma to the head. The encephalopathy symptoms can include behavioral problems, mood problems, and problems with thinking.
This highly poisonous member of the carrot family can grow to nearly 8 feet tall, with hollow, maroon-spotted stems and a famously unpleasant odor — what plant is it?
Conium maculatum (British English) or poison hemlock (in North America), is a highly poisonous flowering plant and a nitrophile weed species in the carrot family Apiaceae.
Nearly every genus in this taxonomic family of armadillos is extinct, except for one genus that still includes eight living species today. Name the family?
Dasypodidae is a family of mostly extinct genera of armadillos.
What flying insect, of which about 3,000 species exist, is known for its large compound eyes, two pairs of transparent wings, and often iridescent, metallic body coloration?
Dragonfly is a flying insect belonging to the infraorder Anisoptera below the order Odonata.
This discipline systematically applies natural science and mathematics to design solutions like bridges, pacemakers, and spacecraft under real-world constraints. What field is it?
Engineering is the practice of systematically applying natural science and mathematics to design and improve systems, devices, or processes that solve problems under constraints.
Colloquially called 'squirting,' this phenomenon involves fluid from the Skene's gland and is physiologically distinct from coital incontinence — what is it?
Female ejaculation is characterized as an expulsion of fluid from the Skene's gland at the lower end of the urethra during or before an orgasm.
This American video game businessman dropped out of Harvard to join Microsoft, where he worked on early Windows and a Doom port, before co-founding Valve Corporation in 1996 — who is he?
Gabe Newell (born November 3, 1962), also known by his nickname GabeN, is an American video game developer and businessman.
Comprising about 50 species native to tropical regions worldwide, this genus produces roughly 80% of the world's natural fiber and doubles as an oilseed crop — which genus?
Gossypium is a genus of flowering plants in the tribe Gossypieae of the mallow family, Malvaceae, from which cotton is harvested.

One of the first plants ever spun into fiber some 50,000 years ago, which fast-growing Cannabis sativa cultivar is grown for rope, textiles, paper, biofuel and food rather than its psychoactive punch?
Hemp is a plant in the botanical class of Cannabis sativa cultivars grown specifically for industrial and consumable use.

This large insect order includes sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants, with more than 150,000 described species, many of whose females have an egg-laying organ often modified into a stinger — what is it called?
Hymenoptera is a large order of insects, comprising the sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants.
This mild oxidizing agent and Lewis acid, with the formula FeCl3, is commonly used to purify water and to etch metal surfaces — which compound is it?
Iron(III) chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula FeCl3. The anhydrous derivative is a Lewis acid, while all forms are mild oxidizing agents.
This Confederate veteran and pharmacist sold the rights to his 1886 beverage recipe to Asa Griggs Candler for about $2,300 shortly before he died — who is he?
John Stith Pemberton (July 8, 1831 - August 16, 1888) was an American pharmacist, chemist, and Confederate States Army officer who is best known as the inventor of Coca-Cola.
Originally a water-retrieving gun dog from Italy's Po Delta marshes, this breed later became prized for hunting truffles once its wetland habitat was drained — what breed is it?
Lagotto Romagnolo is an Italian breed of dog.
Named after a pioneer of sterile surgery, this genus of rod-shaped bacteria can multiply even at refrigerator temperatures and causes a rare but serious foodborne illness — what is it?
Listeria is a genus of bacteria that acts as an intracellular parasite in mammals.
Formed from two glucose units linked by an alpha(1→4) bond, which disaccharide, a reducing sugar unlike sucrose, is released when starch breaks down during malting?
Maltose (or), also known as maltobiose or malt sugar, is a disaccharide formed from two units of glucose joined with an (14) bond.
More than 80% of cases trace to asbestos exposure, and it grows from the thin lining covering the lungs and other organs — which cancer is it?
Mesothelioma is a type of cancer that develops from the thin layer of tissue that covers many of the internal organs (known as the mesothelium).
This genus of edible sac fungi has a honeycomb-like cap of ridges and pits, is prized in French and Catalan cooking, and turns toxic if eaten raw or undercooked. What fungus is this?
Morchella is a genus of edible sac fungi closely related to anatomically simpler cup fungi in the order Pezizales (division Ascomycota).

Encompassing three distinct genetic conditions marked by nervous-system tumors, one type brings café au lait skin spots and scoliosis while another causes early-onset hearing loss and cataracts — which condition?
Neurofibromatosis (NF) refers to a group of three distinct genetic conditions in which tumors grow in the nervous system.
Which applied-math discipline, born from pre-WWII military planning and overlapping heavily with industrial engineering, hunts for the maximum profit or minimum cost in real-world problems?

Operations research (British), often shortened to the initialism OR, is a branch of applied mathematics that deals with the development and application of analytical methods to improve management and decision-making.
This Scottish biologist-turned-town-planner coined the word 'conurbation' and his work contains one of the earliest versions of 'think globally, act locally.' Who was he?
Patrick Geddes (2 October 1854 - 17 April 1932) was a Scottish biologist, sociologist, Comtean positivist, geographer, philanthropist and pioneering town planner.
This genus of spiders in the family Ctenidae is found mainly in northern South America, with a single species ranging into Central America — name this genus?
Phoneutria is a genus of spiders in the family Ctenidae.

Native to most of the Northern Hemisphere, this genus of 25 to 30 deciduous tree species includes poplars, aspens, and cottonwoods, one of which was the first tree ever fully DNA-sequenced — which genus?
Populus is a genus of 25-30 species of deciduous flowering plants in the family Salicaceae, native to most of the Northern Hemisphere.
This yellow-white fluid forms at sites of infection and inflammation — when trapped in tissue it's called an abscess, and near the skin's surface a pimple — name the substance?
Pus is an exudate, typically white-yellow, yellow, or yellow-brown, formed at the site of inflammation during infections, regardless of cause.
Also known as vitamin B2, this nutrient builds two key coenzymes for energy metabolism and may, taken orally, cut down on migraine headaches in adults — what is it?
Riboflavin is a vitamin found in food and sold as a dietary supplement.
Having coded his first game in high school and studied computer science in Tokyo, this man went on to lead Nintendo by championing fun over raw horsepower — who is he?
Satoru Iwata (December 6, 1959 - July 11, 2015) was a Japanese businessman, video game programmer and producer.
Element number 14 is a tetravalent non-metal sometimes called a metalloid, prized for the transistors and integrated circuits it makes possible — which one is it?
Silicon is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
A self-taught Indian genius of infinite series and number theory, he initially struggled to interest established mathematicians because his methods were so unfamiliar — who was he?
Srinivasa Ramanujan (22 December 1887 - 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
Deriving its name from a French word for crushed oak bark used in hide-curing, this class of astringent plant compounds binds to and precipitates proteins and other organic molecules — what is it?
Tannin (or tannoids) are a class of astringent, polyphenolic biomolecules that bind to and precipitate proteins and various other organic compounds including amino acids and alkaloids.
This genus of about 30 tree and shrub species is native across the temperate Northern Hemisphere, with its greatest diversity found in Asia — what genus is it?
Tilia is a genus of about 30 species of trees or bushes, native throughout most of the temperate Northern Hemisphere.
What is the medical term for having dangerously high levels of urea in the blood, typically caused by kidney failure?

Uremia is the condition of having high levels of urea in the blood. It is the signs, symptoms and results from laboratory tests which result from inadequate excretory, regulatory, and endocrine function of the kidneys.
These big cetaceans — everything in the group except dolphins and porpoises — count the hippopotamus as their closest living relative on land. What are they?
Whale are a widely distributed and diverse group of fully aquatic placental marine mammals.
This Danish physicist shared the 1975 Nobel for work on the structure of the atomic nucleus — making him and his famous father one of the rare parent-child pairs to each win the prize. Who was he?
Native to the arid Americas, most rosettes of this succulent genus flower gloriously just once before dying, earning one species the nickname 'century plant' — what genus is it?
Though commonly called a nut, this tree's fruit is technically a drupe with a hard shell surrounding an edible seed, closely related to the peach — which food is it?
Almond: Species of nut. The fruit of the almond is a drupe, consisting of an outer hull and a hard shell with the seed, which is not a true nut.
Despite helping develop the Soviet Union's thermonuclear weapons, this physicist won the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize for his human-rights activism and was later persecuted as a dissident — who was he?
Andrei Sakharov: Soviet nuclear physicist and human rights activist (1921–1989)
The average adult sheds 50 to 70 billion cells a day through this tidy, programmed cell death — named from a Greek word for 'falling off' — quite unlike messy, traumatic necrosis. What is it?
Apoptosis: Form of programmed cell death. Because apoptosis cannot stop once it has begun, it is a highly regulated process.
Driven by elevated LDL cholesterol, this chronic inflammatory disease builds plaque lesions inside artery walls and can lead to stroke or coronary trouble — what is it?
Atherosclerosis: Inflammatory disease involving a buildup of lesions in the walls of arteries.
Originating in Central Africa, this hunting dog breed doesn't bark but makes an unusual yodel-like sound instead, earning it a nickname — what breed is it?
Basenji: Central African breed of dog. The Fédération Cynologique Internationale places it in the Spitz and "primitive types" categories, while the American Kennel Club classifies it as a hound.

Named after two French physicists who discovered it in 1820, this equation in magnetostatics relates a magnetic field to the strength, direction, and distance of an electric current — which physics rule?
Biot–Savart law: Law of classical electromagnetism.
This rigid organ not only supports the body and enables movement but also manufactures both red and white blood cells and stores essential minerals — what is it?
Bone: Rigid organs of the skeleton of vertebrates.

Marketed as Wellbutrin, this atypical antidepressant doubles as a stop-smoking aid and stands out for not causing sexual dysfunction or weight gain — what is this norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor?
Bupropion: Medication mainly used for depression and smoking cessation.
Called 'rockmelon' in Australia and 'spanspek' in South Africa, this orange-fleshed true melon goes by yet another name in North America — what fruit is it?
Cantaloupe: Variety of melon. Originally, cantaloup referred to the true cantaloupe or European cantaloupe with non- to slightly netted and often ribbed rind.
Sold under the brand name Rocephin, this injectable third-generation antibiotic treats everything from meningitis to gonorrhea — which drug?
Ceftriaxone: Antibiotic medication. Ceftriaxone, sold under the brand name Rocephin, is a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.

First recorded in the 3rd-to-5th-century manuscript Sunzi Suanjing, this number-theory result lets you deduce what's left over after dividing by a product of coprime numbers, just from the leftovers after dividing by each one — which principle?
Chinese remainder theorem: About simultaneous modular congruences.
Native to Indonesia's Maluku Islands, these aromatic flower buds flavor your food but also turn up in toothpaste and soaps — what spice are they?
Clove: Spice made from flower buds.
Often defined as the transmission of information, this concept is famously modeled as a source encoding a message, sending it through a channel, and a receiver decoding it — what is it?
Communication: Transmission of information. Models of communication are simplified overviews of its main components and their interactions.
A group of these black birds is famously called a 'murder,' and their larger cousins are known as ravens — what bird is this?
Crow: Index of animals with the same common name.
The second jet fighter to enter RAF service and the first powered by a single jet engine, this twin-boom aircraft flew with the Halford Goblin turbojet — which aircraft?

De Havilland Vampire: Fighter aircraft; first single-engine jet in RAF service. The de Havilland DH100 Vampire is a British jet fighter developed and manufactured by the de Havilland Aircraft Company.
This category of mental health conditions involves an unconscious defense mechanism that fragments consciousness, memory, and identity to protect against traumatic stress — what is it called?
Dissociative disorder: Set of mental health conditions.
A pregnancy complication where the embryo attaches outside the uterus, classically presenting with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. What is this condition?
Ectopic pregnancy: Female reproductive system health issue.
A sympathomimetic stimulant often used to keep blood pressure up during anesthesia, this drug has also been tried for asthma, narcolepsy, and obesity — what is it?

Ranging from Northern Europe through Siberia to the Himalayas, this medium-sized wild cat is one of only four living species in its genus and can be found at elevations up to 5,500 meters — what animal is this?
Eurasian lynx: Species of medium-sized cat native to Eurasia.

Named for the physicist who reportedly asked 'but where is everybody?' at Los Alamos in 1950, this puzzle questions why we've found no evidence of alien civilizations despite the odds favoring them — what's it called?
Fermi paradox: Discrepancy of the lack of evidence for alien life despite its apparent likelihood.
Alongside James Watson, this English scientist co-authored the 1953 Nature paper unveiling DNA's double helix and later coined the phrase 'central dogma' — who is he?
Francis Crick: English physicist and biologist (1916–2004)

Published by Einstein in 1916 as a refinement of Newton's law of gravitation, this geometric framework describes gravity as curved spacetime, summed up by Wheeler as 'space-time tells matter how to move; matter tells space-time how to curve'?
General relativity: Theory of gravitation as curved spacetime. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Despite its common name, this Eurasian wolf-like canid is more closely related to wolves and coyotes than to its African namesakes — what animal is it?
Published in 1931 by an Austrian logician, these two results proved that any consistent axiom system for arithmetic will always contain true statements it cannot prove — what are they called?
Gödel's incompleteness theorems: Limitative results in mathematical logic.

This French mathematician reinvented what it means to find the area under a curve, publishing his sweeping new theory of integration in a 1902 dissertation titled "Integral, length, area." Who was he?
Strongly associated with human habitation and now the most widely distributed wild bird on Earth thanks to introductions across multiple continents, this small brown-and-black bird is which species?
House sparrow: Species of bird. The house sparrow (Passer domesticus) is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in most parts of the world.
Apple's proprietary mobile operating system, originally called iPhone OS, was unveiled in January 2007 alongside which product?
iOS, formerly iPhone OS, is a proprietary mobile operating system created by Apple for its iPhone line. It was unveiled in January 2007 alongside the first-generation iPhone and released that June.
An English polymath who was also an alchemist and theologian, he shares credit with Leibniz for inventing calculus and wrote the Principia — who is he?

A former Chicago options trader with finance degrees but no PhD, this entrepreneur co-founded a dot-com company whose peer-reviewed project evolved into the world's largest free encyclopedia — who is he?
Its subfamily name literally means 'large foot,' it's native to Australia and New Guinea, and a 2019 government tally counted some 42.8 million of them in harvest areas. Which marsupial?
Kangaroo: Marsupial of the family Macropodidae.
Also called the Mediterranean black widow, this venomous spider is common throughout the Mediterranean region and central Asia — what species is it?

Latrodectus tredecimguttatus: Species of spider. Latrodectus tredecimguttatus, also known as the Mediterranean black widow or the European black widow, is a species in the genus Latrodectus of the widow spiders.
This Australian speech and language therapist and amateur stage actor helped King George VI manage his stammer — who is he?
Lionel Logue: Australian speech and language therapist (1880–1953)
This flowering legume genus boasts over 199 species and has become such a successful invasive spreader in Iceland that it's now considered an ecological problem — which genus?
With horn-shaped fins on its head and one of the highest brain-to-body ratios of any fish, this filter-feeding giant may even recognize itself in a mirror — which creature?
Sold under the brand name Mobic, this NSAID in the oxicam family blocks COX-2 more strongly than COX-1 and ranked 27th among the most prescribed US medications in 2023. What drug is it?
Developed for the Soviet Union, this swept-wing jet fighter dominated early dogfights in the Korean War and prompted the US to rush its F-86 Sabre into combat — which aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15: Soviet fighter aircraft. The MiG-15 was one of the first successful jet fighters to incorporate swept wings to perform near Mach 1.
With roughly 200 species across 16 genera, this family of elongated fish is almost exclusively marine, with a name traced back through Portuguese and Latin to a Greek word — which family?
Moray eel: Family of fishes. Moray eels, or Muraenidae, are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.
The only mammal that's essentially cold-blooded, this burrowing "sand puppy" of the Horn of Africa also lives in an insect-like colony with a single breeding queen — what creature is it?
Sold under the brand name Macrobid, this antibacterial drug treats lower urinary tract infections but isn't effective against kidney infections. What is it?
Nitrofurantoin: Antibacterial drug. Nitrofurantoin, sold under the brand name Macrobid among others, is an antibacterial medication of the nitrofuran class.

Sold under the brand name Zofran, this serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist prevents chemotherapy- and surgery-related nausea without the dopamine-blocking side effects that cause muscle restlessness — what is this drug?
Ondansetron: Medication to prevent nausea and vomiting.
Known for its fragrant leaves used to flavor dishes across Southeast Asia, Sri Lanka and Hainanese cuisine, this member of the screwpine genus is prized in many Asian kitchens — which plant?
Pandanus amaryllifolius: Species of tropical plant.
This genus of fungi is responsible for both a groundbreaking antibiotic and the mold that ripens certain blue cheeses — which genus?
Enclosed in a papery husk derived from its calyx, this nightshade genus includes the tomatillo and Cape gooseberry among its edible-fruited species — which genus?

The most common hormonal disorder in women of reproductive age, it's diagnosed by two of three signs — irregular periods, high testosterone, or many antral follicles — despite a name that misleadingly implies true cysts. What's its newer name?
Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: Hormonal disorder in women. The exact cause of PMOS remains uncertain.
Native to Eurasia and known by the common names 'cherry plum' and 'myrobalan plum,' this species is thought to be a parent of the cultivated plum — what is it, scientifically?
Prunus cerasifera: Species of plum. Native to Eurasia and naturalized elsewhere, P. cerasifera is believed to be one of the parents of the cultivated plum.
Built from bases including uracil, adenine, guanine, and cytosine, this molecule can serve as a template for building proteins or catalyze reactions itself — what is it?
RNA: Family of large biological molecules.
One of the largest land megafauna left, this odd-toed ungulate has five surviving species — two in Africa, three across South and Southeast Asia — and a name meaning "nose-horned." What is it?
Co-founder and first president of Mattel, she dreamed up a certain doll in 1959 and was later portrayed in the 2023 Barbie film — who was she?
Ruth Handler: American business magnate and inventor (1916–2002)
Usually forming an S- or C-shaped curve with a rotational twist, this sideways irregular curvature of the spine sits alongside kyphosis and lordosis among the spine's abnormal curves. What is it?
Scoliosis: Left-right asymmetry of the spine's curvature.

This medical condition of inadequate blood flow to body tissues comes in four flavors — hypovolemic, cardiogenic, obstructive, and distributive — and can progress to confusion or cardiac arrest if untreated — what is it called?
Shock (circulatory): Medical condition of insufficient blood flow. Shock is the state of insufficient blood flow to the tissues of the body as a result of problems with the circulatory system.

Self-taught from her father's library and writing to Gauss and Lagrange under a male pseudonym, this French mathematician pioneered elasticity theory and laid groundwork for Fermat's Last Theorem — who was she?
Sophie Germain: French mathematician, physicist, and philosopher.
This retired American physician turned ufologist founded both a center for extraterrestrial-intelligence study and a project pushing for the release of classified UFO information — who is he?
This Polish tax advisor turned politician placed third in the 2025 presidential election while chairing the libertarian New Hope party — who is he?
Sławomir Mentzen: Polish economist and politician (born 1986)
This large mass of gray matter sits between the cerebral cortex and the midbrain, relaying sensory and motor signals to the cortex while regulating sleep and alertness — what is this brain structure?
Thalamus: Structure within the brain. It has several functions, such as the relaying of sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex and the regulation of consciousness, sleep, and alertness.
Also known as the Mexican husk tomato, this nightshade fruit has been cultivated since pre-Columbian times and is the key ingredient in salsa verde — what is it?

This large flatfish native to the Northeast Atlantic, Baltic, and Mediterranean gave its name to a 1990s fishing dispute between Canada and Spain, even though a different species was the real catch at stake — which fish?
Turbot: Species of flatfish in the family Scophthalmidae.
Born in 1946, this German facilitator and non-fiction writer built a career exploring esoteric subjects until her death in 2011 — who was she?
Vera F. Birkenbihl: German facilitator, writer. Vera Felicitas Birkenbihl (26 April 1946 - 3 December 2011) was a German facilitator, non-fiction writer, and esoteric.
First isolated in 1669 by alchemist Henning Brand, this waxy, translucent form of an element glows faintly green in the dark and ignites spontaneously in air — which substance?
Sold under the brand name Ambien, which nonbenzodiazepine 'Z-drug' cuts the time to fall asleep by about fifteen minutes?
The symbol for scandium is Sc. Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
The symbol for hydrogen is H. Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.

James Acaster is a comedian. James William Acaster (born 9 January 1985) is an English comedian, presenter, podcaster and actor.
In what year was Michael Caine born?
Michael Caine: Sir Michael Caine (born Maurice Joseph Micklewhite; 14 March 1933) is an English retired actor.
In what year was Tobey Maguire born?
Tobey Maguire: Tobias Vincent Maguire (born June 27, 1975) is an American actor and film producer.
In what year was Mia Khalifa born?
Mia Khalifa (Arabic: ميا خليفة, born February 10, 1993) is a Lebanese-American media personality and former pornographic film actress.
In what year was Shannen Doherty born?
Shannen Doherty: Shannen Maria Doherty (April 12, 1971 – July 13, 2024) was an American actress.
